records.name: Sharon Pierce
records.notes: President since July 2016; college now branded Minneapolis College. Named president of the year by ACCT in 2020. Predecessor(s) not documented in available online sources; more history likely exists in Minnesota State system archives.

records.name: Beverly Walker-Griffea
records.notes: Seventh president of Mott Community College (Aug 2014-2024); first female and first African American president in the college's history. Now President Emeritus.

records.name: Shaunda Richardson-Snell
records.notes: Served as interim president for nearly a year before being appointed permanent president in May 2025. Prior background includes executive roles at General Motors and Trinity Health.

records.name: Daria Willis
records.notes: Served July 2019-January 2022 as EvCC's first African American president before departing for another presidency.

records.name: Chemene Crawford
records.notes: Began July 1, 2023 on a three-year contract (~$281K salary); previously president of North Seattle College. An interim likely bridged the gap between Willis's Jan 2022 departure and Crawford's 2023 start, but that person was not identified in available sources.

records.name: Para M. Jones
records.notes: Served as one of SCC's early presidents after the Spartanburg Technical College to Spartanburg Community College transition.

records.name: Henry C. Giles, Jr.
records.notes: Sixth president of SCC, retired in 2020.

records.name: Michael Mikota
records.notes: Named seventh president of SCC effective July 13, 2020; previously led Central Carolina Technical College in Sumter, SC since 2017.

records.name: Angel Reyna
records.notes: A former migrant farmworker and first-generation college graduate, Reyna has led Madera Community College (a young institution, formerly a center of Reedley/State Center CCD, independently accredited circa 2021) since its early years; selected for Aspen Institute's New Presidents Fellowship in 2021. No predecessor identified since Madera is a newly independent college; he is effectively its founding/first president.

records.name: Michael Claire
records.nextRoleInstitution: San Mateo County Community College District
records.notes: Left the Cañada College presidency to become Chancellor of the San Mateo County Community College District, prompting Kim Lopez's interim appointment in 2021.

records.name: Kim Lopez
records.priorTitle: Interim President (previously VP of Student Services)
records.notes: Served as interim president of Cañada College from August 2021, converted to permanent president July 1, 2022. Previously VP of student services and acting/interim president at College of San Mateo.

records.name: David C. Hespe
records.notes: Fourth president of the college (then Burlington County College).

records.name: Paul Drayton
records.notes: Fifth president; removed from post in September 2017 amid a discrimination-allegation investigation, placed on paid administrative leave.

records.name: Michael A. Cioce
records.notes: First-generation college student who rose through RCBC leadership as VP and acting president before being named permanent (sixth) president in 2018.

records.name: Pamela Edington
records.notes: First woman to serve as president of Dutchess Community College.

records.name: Peter Grant Jordan
records.notes: Began August 2, 2021; first person of color to serve as president of DCC. College's first president (1957-) was James F. Hall; full mid-century succession not detailed in available sources.

records.name: Peter J. Boylan
records.notes: Major General; longest-serving president in GMC history (nearly 21 years), credited with restoring the college's financial stability. Later President Emeritus until his death.

records.name: William B. Caldwell IV
records.priorTitle: Commanding General, U.S. Army North (Fifth Army)
records.notes: 21st president, selected after a six-month national search; retired Lieutenant General.

records.name: Terrence J. McKenrick
records.notes: Retired Major General; named 22nd president, assumed office July 1, 2025, succeeding Caldwell.

records.name: Richard Sanchez
records.notes: First tenure as president 1998-2013 (retired); oversaw major enrollment growth, named fastest-growing public two-year college in the nation.

records.name: Barbara Kavalier
records.notes: Navarro's sixth president and first female chief executive; departed in 2016 to lead another institution.

records.name: Kevin G. Fegan
records.notes: Current District President since September 2018; between Kavalier's 2016 departure and Fegan's 2018 arrival, Richard Sanchez returned for a brief second stint (2016-2018).

records.name: Jack Oharah
records.notes: Long-serving president of Edmonds Community College, 1996-2010.

records.name: Amit B. Singh
records.notes: Fifth president of Edmonds College, joined June 2018; over 30 years of higher education experience.

records.name: Mojdeh Mehdizadeh
records.notes: 12th permanent president of Contra Costa College; removed from post in January 2018.

records.name: Katrina VanderWoude
records.notes: Hired as permanent president May 31, 2018; placed on administrative leave May 28, 2019 pending investigation and subsequently resigned. Interim leaders (reportedly including Damon A. Bell and Tia Robinson-Cooper) bridged the gap until 2022, though exact dates were not confirmed in available sources.

records.name: Kimberly R. Rogers
records.notes: Became acting president in June 2022 (having joined CCC as VP of Instruction in Jan 2021) and was named the 15th permanent president when the 4CD Governing Board ratified her contract on June 14, 2023.

records.name: Ismael Sosa, Jr.
records.notes: Named president of Southwest Texas Junior College (Uvalde, TX) in 1999; retired July 31, 2013 after nearly 15 years.

records.name: Hector Gonzales
records.notes: CONFIRMATION GAP: Search snippets place Dr. Hector Gonzales as president of Southwest Texas Junior College as of the 2020-2021 academic year (following Sosa's 2013 retirement), but the college's website (swtjc.edu) returned server errors throughout this research session, so his exact start date and whether he remains president in 2026 could not be verified. Needs direct follow-up via swtjc.edu or a press database.

records.name: Kevin Eaton
records.notes: Referenced as Weatherford College president in a 2010 alumni publication; exact tenure dates not confirmed in available sources (a predecessor named Don Huff was referenced in a 1998 document).

records.name: Tod Allen Farmer
records.priorTitle: Chief of Staff / Dept. Head, Educational Leadership and Policy Studies
records.notes: 20th president of Weatherford College since 2018; first WC alumnus to hold the role; spent 12 years in administration at Tarleton State University prior.

records.name: Harvey Haynes
records.notes: President Emeritus; appointed after the death of A-B Tech's first president, Thomas Simpson.

records.name: K. Ray Bailey
records.notes: Listed as President/CEO in an institutional profile; served between Betty Young and John Gossett, but exact tenure years were not confirmed in available sources.

records.name: John D. Gossett
records.notes: Seventh president of A-B Tech, joined July 2020 (named March 19, 2020); previously president of McDowell Technical Community College in Marion, NC. Betty Young also served as a president between Haynes and Gossett, exact dates unconfirmed.

records.name: Lisa Skari
records.notes: Current president since 2018; joined the WICHE Commission in 2023.

records.name: Manny Cabral
records.priorTitle: Interim Chancellor (28-year Leeward CC employee: faculty senate vice chair, math/science division chair)
records.notes: Served as Interim Chancellor from March 2007, converted to permanent Chancellor June 1, 2008; worked at Leeward CC for 28 years total before/during his chancellorship.

records.name: Carlos Peñaloza
records.priorInstitution: Metropolitan Community College (Kansas City) / Saint Luke's College of Health Sciences
records.notes: 12th CEO/Chancellor of Leeward Community College, became chancellor July 1, 2019; extensive background in biomedical research and higher ed leadership.

records.name: Toni Hopper Pendergrass
records.notes: President of San Juan College (Farmington, NM) since July 2, 2012. Previously VP for Learning at San Jacinto College and held roles at El Centro College (Dallas). Predecessor not identified in available sources.
